The bound for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_3</annotation></semantics></math> uses the next derivative, the fourth: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>10</mn><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{10}{4!}(0.5)^4</annotation></semantics></math>.

Divide by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>!</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4! = 24</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>10</mn><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{10}{4!}(0.5)^4</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10(0.5)^4</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Which statement shows that <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_3(0.5)</annotation></semantics></math> approximates <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(0.5)</annotation></semantics></math> with an error less than <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.03</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.03</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|f(0.5) - P_3(0.5)\right|</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>192</mn></mfrac><mo><</mo><mn>0.03</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{5}{192} < 0.03</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mn>10</mn><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>3</mn></msup><mo><</mo><mn>0.03</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|f(0.5) - P_3(0.5)\right| \le \frac{10}{3!}(0.5)^3 < 0.03</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mn>6</mn><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>4</mn></msup><mo><</mo><mn>0.03</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|f(0.5) - P_3(0.5)\right| \le \frac{6}{4!}(0.5)^4 < 0.03</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>192</mn></mfrac><mo><</mo><mn>0.03</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|f(0.5) - P_3(0.5)\right| \le \frac{5}{192} < 0.03</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: What do the estimate and the bound together say about <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(0.5)</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>192</mn></mfrac><mo>≤</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>192</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{7}{4} - \frac{5}{192} \le f(0.5) \le \frac{7}{4} + \frac{5}{192}</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>192</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(0.5) = \frac{7}{4} + \frac{5}{192}</annotation></semantics></math>, the estimate plus the bound

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>≤</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>192</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{7}{4} \le f(0.5) \le \frac{7}{4} + \frac{5}{192}</annotation></semantics></math>, above the estimate

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>192</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(0.5) \le \frac{5}{192}</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Which choice of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>, a bound on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">‴</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|f'''(z)\right|</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0 \le z \le \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, is justified?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M = 1</annotation></semantics></math>: the third derivative at the center is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^0 = 1</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M = 2</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>z</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^z</annotation></semantics></math> increases, so its largest value is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{1/2}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo><</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{1/2} < 2</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1.284</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M = 1.284</annotation></semantics></math>: the value at the middle of the interval

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M = \frac{1}{8}</annotation></semantics></math>: the value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x^3}{3!}</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_2\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The quadratic term is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x^2}{2} = \frac{1}{8}</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: With <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, find the Lagrange error bound for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|e^{1/2} - P_2\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right|</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That uses <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, the value at the center; the bound needs the largest value on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, \frac{1}{2}]</annotation></semantics></math>.

Divide by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>!</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3! = 6</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2!</annotation></semantics></math>: the bound for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_2</annotation></semantics></math> uses the third derivative.

items.q: A calculator gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.6487</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{1/2} \approx 1.6487</annotation></semantics></math>. How does the actual error compare with the bound <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>24</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{24}</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: The actual error, about <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.024</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.024</annotation></semantics></math>, is below the bound, as it has to be
The actual error equals the bound, about <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.042</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.042</annotation></semantics></math>, as expected

The actual error is larger than the bound, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M = 2</annotation></semantics></math> was too small

The two are not comparable, since the bound used <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M = 2</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Which is the Lagrange error bound for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_n(x)</annotation></semantics></math>, the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>th-degree Taylor polynomial for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> about <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = a</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>!</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\max\left|f^{(n)}(z)\right|}{n!}|x - a|^n</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>!</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\max\left|f^{(n+1)}(z)\right|}{(n+1)!}|x - a|^{n+1}</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>!</mo></mrow></mfrac><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\left|f^{(n+1)}(a)\right|}{(n+1)!}\left|x - a\right|^{n+1}</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo>⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\max\left|f^{(n+1)}(z)\right| \cdot |x - a|^{n+1}</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_3(x) = x - \frac{x^3}{6}</annotation></semantics></math> approximates <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x</annotation></semantics></math>.
